units.title: An idempotency key lets the server recognise a retry
units.claim: An idempotency key is a unique value a client attaches to a request so the server can tell a retry of the same operation from a new one.
units.explanation: The core concept. Everything else in the source is how it is used and where it stops working.

omission.reason: It is the subject of the source.

units.title: A completed key gets its stored result back
units.claim: When a request with the key has already completed, the server returns the stored result instead of running the operation again.
units.explanation: The mechanism that makes a retry harmless.
mustPreserve: only for a request that already completed

units.title: Protection lasts only while results are kept (24 hours)
units.claim: Keys protect against duplicates only while the server remembers them; stored results expire after 24 hours, after which a retry is treated as a new payment.
units.explanation: The bound on the mechanism. Without it the reader would believe retries are always safe.

paraphrase.note: The number and its unit stay exact.

omission.reason: A critical limitation of the main claim.

units.title: A reused key with a different amount must be rejected
units.claim: A key does not make two different requests safe: a reused key with a different amount must be rejected, not answered with the old result.
units.explanation: The second bound on the mechanism: the key identifies one operation, not any request.

units.title: Example: a dropped checkout response is retried safely
units.claim: A checkout client sends Idempotency-Key 7f3c-91ab, the connection drops, the client retries with the same key, and the server returns the original confirmation, so the customer is charged once.
units.explanation: Illustrates ku.replay. Supporting, not a separate idea.

related.note: The example illustrates the mechanism (edge runs mechanism → example).

omission.reason: Supporting; may be shortened, but if shown the identifiers stay exact.

units.title: Retries are safe within a bounded window, not always
units.claim: Idempotency keys make retries safe within a bounded window; they are not a general guarantee against duplicate operations.
units.explanation: The takeaway, which carries its own limit.

mustNotClaim.claim: Idempotency keys always prevent duplicate charges.
mustNotClaim.why: The source bounds the protection to a 24-hour window and to identical requests.

mustNotClaim.claim: A reused key returns the original result even if the amount differs.
mustNotClaim.why: The source says such a request must be rejected.
Not stated; the source explicitly denies a general guarantee.
